From: Anna Sokolov <anna@helixone.com>

Subject: Question: EU-only processing & operator access for PII workloads

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — HelixOne is evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will process EU patient data (PII, pseudonymized). Before we move to the legal review, legal and security need firm answers on a few items:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that all inference and training-related processing for our tenant will run only in EU jurisdictions (no US egress) under the proposed setup?
2) With SCCs in place, what operator access controls do you enforce? We need an operator access model that:
   - Restricts human access to EU-based operators only, or
   - Provides verifiable audit logs and just-in-time access with customer approval.
3) Backups & snapshots: are backups kept in-region? If not, how do you handle export and deletion requests?
4) Evidence: what artifacts can you provide for procurement and our security team? (SCCs appendix, attestation of in-region processing, proof-of-deletion for test data, audit logs).

Target timeline: procurement wants these answers this week so the legal team can start redlining. If helpful, I can share the HelixOne security questionnaire.

Appreciate any quick clarity you can provide.

—Anna
Anna Sokolov
Head of Cloud Security, HelixOne

Hi Anna — great questions. High-level answers below; we can follow with a one-hour technical walkthrough + attestation package.

Summary (short answers):
- EU-only processing: Yes for our Private and Dedicated EU deployments. We run inference and any persistent storage in customer-chosen EU regions. For our Hosted tier, we can route and constrain processing to EU regions under a Dedicated/Private commitment; otherwise, Hosted may use multi-region routing which wouldn’t meet your requirement.
- SCCs: We will execute the standard EU SCCs (EU Commission template) and provide the SCCs appendix for HelixOne to review.
- Operator access: We support two controls: (A) Dedicated/Private with operator restrictions (customer-managed networking + in-region operator pools) and (B) Hosted w/ policy-based role restrictions + JIT access and approval flows. For high-assurance customers we can provide:
  * In-region operator pool (operators physically located and contracted in EU) tied to Dedicated/Private deployments.
  * Audit trails, session recording (where permitted), and tamper-evident logs shipped to your log sink (or collaborator-managed SIEM).
- Backups/snapshots: For Dedicated/Private, backups and snapshots are kept in-region by default. For Hosted we will provide options — if you require in-region-only backups we recommend Dedicated/Private.

Next steps I propose:
1) Exchange HelixOne security questionnaire (we can pre-fill common answers).
2) Schedule a technical walkthrough (30–45m) with Karthik (security) and Soojin (ops) to show the operator access controls and backup architecture.
3) Deliver an attestation bundle: SCCs appendix, in-region processing attestation, example audit logs, and a proof-of-deletion sample.

Attachments: redwood-sccs-appendix-v1.2.pdf (SCCs + rider), in-region-operator-playbook.pdf (operational controls summary)

If that plan works I can have the attestation bundle to you within 48 hours after the walkthrough. Available times: Apr 11 16:00 CET or Apr 12 09:30 CET.

—Irene

Irene / Soojin — quick notes to align before the walkthrough with HelixOne: 

- Operator geography: For Dedicated/Private we can promise EU-based operator pools via contractual language + location controls. We cannot guarantee a named person list, but we can provide supplier attestations and location-based HR records under NDA.
- JIT and approvals: We have a JIT flow that requires a ticket approval from a designated HelixOne approver for any elevated session. That flow logs the approver and timestamps and emits to a dedicated audit stream.
- Audit evidence: Plan to include
  * example session log (redacted)
  * proof-of-deletion sample (S3 delete + archive manifest)
  * KMS key policy excerpt showing CMK scoping per customer (for Private customers)
- Backups: For Dedicated/Private, snapshot lifecycle policy keeps data in EU by default and retention is configurable. For Hosted we can run a dedicated EU tenancy but need contract-level commitment.

I'll prepare the three artifacts (session-log-example.log, proof-of-deletion-manifest.csv, kms-policy-snippet.txt) and put them in the Drive link Irene referenced. Soojin — please confirm the earliest time you can join the walkthrough.

—Karthik

Call summary / commitments:
- Deployment: We recommend Redwood Dedicated in EU-west-1 for the pilot. This will pin inference and storage to EU infrastructure.
- Contractual safeguards: Redwood will execute SCCs and include an in-region processing rider in the DPA. See attached redwood-sccs-appendix-v1.2.pdf and sccs-implementation-summary.docx.

- Backups & deletion: Backups will be stored in-region and we will provide a proof-of-deletion manifest for any data purge requests. Sample artifacts included.

Attachments included: redwood-sccs-appendix-v1.2.pdf, in-region-operator-playbook.pdf, sccs-implementation-summary.docx
